name: Tank Yard v0.16.0
body:
# Tank Yard v0.16.0

Workshop gates take several conditions, watchers and sequences arrive, navigation suits trackpads, busy servers run lighter, and Tank Yard now runs natively on FreeBSD.

## Map logic

- A trigger can check up to four conditions: a counter, whether a group is shown, how many tanks are inside its area, or the round time. Combine them as All (AND), Any (OR), Not all (NAND), None (NOR) or Just one (XOR).
- A shut gate can send an otherwise signal, which makes it an if/else. New otherwise signals pick a free channel.
- Watchers fire when a counter changes, a group is shown or hidden, or a boss is defeated. Sequence signals the next of a run of channels each time, and Reset triggers lets a group's triggers start afresh.
- Press P for the live Logic tab. It can step, change speed, edit counters, switch groups, send signals and test a boss defeat. Each condition card shows whether it holds and whether the gate is open.
- Logic and Gates are separate palette tabs. Gates holds ready-made AND, OR, XOR and if/else pieces, levers, sequences, watchers and resets. Wires show what each trigger depends on, and labels make room for each other when crowded.
- Scripts can call `reset_map_triggers(group)`, and the bundled Logic Kit adds a Lever bank tool.
- The [logic gates tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/logic-gates-tutorial.md) builds a two-lever vault step by step, and the [video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/logic-gates-tutorial.mp4) shows it in under two minutes.

## Workshop navigation

- Pan (4) moves the view with a plain drag. In Pan, arrows and WASD move the view even with objects selected.
- The Scroll setting chooses Auto, Trackpad or Mouse. With a trackpad, two fingers pan, and Ctrl or Cmd with scrolling zooms around the pointer. Pan and zoom speeds go from 0.25× to 3×, and 100% resets the zoom. The workshop remembers these settings.
- Zoom follows how far you scroll instead of jumping a full step for any movement.
- Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through overlapping objects under the pointer. Resize handles and panel dividers are easier to grab.

## Scrolling everywhere

- Menus, chat, the lobby and mod lists, the mod viewer and the tank tree scroll smoothly with trackpads and step evenly with wheels, on macOS, Windows, Wayland and X11. Ordinary wheels no longer scroll slowly on Wayland.

## Servers

- Projectile, wall and navigation checks skip distant objects. In a local test with 64 players and 24 bots on a maze map, 99th-percentile tick time fell from about 3.3 to 1.8 ms.
- Starting a server lists the addresses players join from this computer, the local network and the internet. Every option has clearer help.
- Linux, macOS and FreeBSD archives include `host-server.sh`, which writes a settings file on first run and then starts the server with it. The systemd unit keeps settings, bans and logs in `/var/lib/tankyard`. The [hosting guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/hosting.md) walks through installing, configuring, opening the port and running a service.

## FreeBSD

- FreeBSD 15 and newer on amd64 get their own build of the game, server, relay and tools, made on FreeBSD itself. Install the sound plugins with `pkg install alsa-plugins`, then run `fetch -o - https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`.
- The game uses X11 and OpenGL with Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. With NVIDIA, it queues one frame ahead, as on Linux. DLSS is available only on Linux and Windows.
- The FreeBSD archive carries an rc.d script that runs the server as its own user, restarts it if it stops, reopens its log when rotated, and can run several named servers.
- The [FreeBSD guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/freebsd.md) covers NVIDIA setup, sound, hosting and building from source.

## Fixes

- Leaving a WebSocket server through the relay reaches the server at once on FreeBSD, instead of after a timeout.
- The installer works without curl on FreeBSD, using `fetch` and `sha256`.

Protocol **25**, as in 0.15. Players on any 0.15 or 0.16 build play together. Maps that use the new logic need a 0.16 server, or 0.16 to play them offline; older servers refuse them with a clear message. Maps without it save exactly as before.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.15.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.15.2

Menus follow your frame limit, frame limits hold their exact rate, and the Arena Workshop tutorial and a full plugin guide now live in the docs.

## Frame rate

- The title screen and menus run at the selected frame limit instead of stopping near 60 fps. With VSync on and no limit, they follow the display's refresh rate. Battery saver still holds games to 60 fps and menus to 30.
- Frame limits now count the time spent presenting each frame and keep a steady schedule, so 60 and 144 fps limits run at 60 and 144 rather than overshooting or falling short. The opening animation uses the same pacing.

## Arena Workshop

- When a plugin tool removes objects and doesn't choose what to select, the selection keeps only objects that still exist.
- The [tutorial video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/arena-workshop-tutorial.mp4) is in the repository's docs, linked from the README and the [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/map-editor.md). Game packages leave it out to keep downloads small.
- The new [editor plugin guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/editor-plugins.md) covers installing plugins, a complete first tool, pack layout, every parameter type, the `ctx` API, coordinates, group and counter allocation, map checks, execution limits, distribution and troubleshooting. A test runs its example exactly as printed.

## Documentation

- Guides, server measurements and earlier release notes are tidied for players, mod authors, hosts and maintainers. The bundled Workshop Toolkit and Logic Kit READMEs link to the plugin guide.

Protocol **25**, as in v0.15.0 and v0.15.1. Clients and servers from those versions play together.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.15.1
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.15.1

Arena Workshop gains Luau plugins, resizable panels, more map logic and an updated tutorial. Voice and snapshot delivery get several fixes.

## Arena Workshop

- Drag the inspector and dock edges to resize them, double-click to reset, or press **\\** to hide the panels. The workshop remembers its layout and view preferences.
- Resize a whole selection with its handles. Hold Shift to keep proportions or Alt to resize around the center. Thin selections keep enough space to drag them. Frame the selection with Shift+F, mirror a copy with M, repeat a move with Ctrl+D, and lock groups while editing around them.
- Enabled, reviewed packs can add Luau tools and map checks in the **Tools** tab. Each tool edits a copy of the map, validates its result and applies it as one undo step. Ctrl+R repeats the last tool. Workshop Toolkit provides repeat, ring, frame, snap and mirror tools. Logic Kit builds switch doors, countdowns and sequences.
- The Check tab includes plugin advice and object budgets. The toolkit's gap check handles touching walls and dense maps.

[Workshop guide](../map-editor.md) · [Plugin API](../modding.md#workshop-plugins) · [Updated tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/releases/download/v0.15.1/arena-workshop-tutorial.mp4)

## Map logic and scripting

- Add While inside, On empty and On destroy triggers. Actions can set counters, choose a random signal, repair or damage tanks, and award points.
- Gate triggers on counter comparisons or group visibility. Calculate supports arithmetic, counter operands, random values and a 0/1 flip. Use **Fire** to test an action directly in the editor preview.
- Script actions raise the Luau `map_event` event. Scripts can read map counters and group visibility, send map signals, change counters, and show or hide groups. Script requests apply on the next simulation tick.
- Malformed counter and random-signal settings are rejected safely, including extreme integer values.

## Voice, networking and bosses

- Voice uses a 48 kbps Opus target, a microphone high-pass filter, a speech lead-in and hangover, adaptive playback buffering, fades and a soft limiter for mixed voices. The server reuses listener calculations across each received batch.
- Late snapshots preserve the newest cached wall geometry. Changed walls repeat in four snapshots, with periodic recovery resends, reducing traffic from maps with moving gates.
- Bastion gains a fortress hull, corner towers and a rotating central gun. Sentinel, Skirmisher and Trapper receive restrained armor details.

Protocol **25**, as in v0.15.0. The server sends clients map geometry with server-side triggers removed, so v0.15.0 players can join a v0.15.1 server using the new logic. Maps and editor plugins using the new APIs require v0.15.1 on the machine running them.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.15.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.15.0

The Arena Workshop gets a rebuilt editor, map logic you can test in place, and two new pads: conveyors and portals.

## Arena Workshop

- Switch between Build, Edit and Delete with 1, 2 and 3. Click to place a cell or drag to draw any size. Turn on Swipe to paint as you drag, or right-click an object to build copies of it.
- Drag across the floor to select a region, double-click to select a whole group, and Alt-drag to leave a copy behind. Turn, flip, align, resize and reorder from the dock or the keyboard, and copy one object's settings onto others. Undo keeps 48 steps.
- Click any value to type an exact number, or edit several objects at once. An object's group can start hidden right from its own panel, and the map id follows the arena's name.
- The Check tab lists anything that would stop a playtest or export and selects each problem on the canvas. Shift+F5 starts a playtest at the pointer, and F1 lists every shortcut.

## Map logic

- Triggers can now fire when a tank leaves an area, on a signal from another trigger, or when one of eight counters reaches a value. New actions send signals, add to counters and drop shapes.
- Limit a trigger to players, bots or one team, and give it a chance and a delay. Hiding a trigger's own group switches it off. Labels and announcements show counters with `{1}` to `{8}`.
- Press P to run the logic inside the editor and hold T to drive a test tank through it. L draws a line from each trigger to what it changes. The Logic palette has presets for plates, timers, signals, counters, goals, shape drops and boss calls.

## Pads

- Conveyors carry tanks along their arrows, and their marks move with the belt. Portals send tanks to an exit marker you drag into place.
- Conveyor and speed effects are predicted on your side, so movement stays smooth online.

## Fixes

- A drag along one grid line builds a block one cell deep instead of an invisible sliver. Grid lines draw evenly at every zoom.
- The Escape that ends a playtest no longer also clears the editor selection. The shortcut list no longer cuts off its descriptions.
- Save and export messages show short workshop paths, and the settings panel scrolls faster.

[Workshop guide](../map-editor.md) · [Map schema](../modding.md#maps)

**Multiplayer update:** This release uses protocol **25**. Upgrade the server and clients together. Versions 0.14 and earlier use an incompatible snapshot and map format.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.14.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.14.0

Build custom arenas in the Arena Workshop, host a community on your own domain, and take on three new bosses.

## Arena Workshop

- Open **Map editor** on the main menu. Build solid cover, pads, spawns, objectives and decorations on a grid. Select, resize, rotate, duplicate, mirror and group objects. Undo and redo keep the last 32 operations.
- Add timed gates, entry triggers, announcements and boss arrivals. Speed, mud, repair, hazard and shelter pads affect the match. Preview and tune particle emitters in the FX tab.
- Playtest with F5 and return with Escape. Save a project, import an existing map pack or copy a built-in arena. Export a ZIP to share or load on a server. The included Switchyard example demonstrates a timed gate and linked effects.

[Workshop guide](../map-editor.md) · [Map schema](../modding.md#maps)

## Community hosting and parties

- Run UDP and WebSocket joins from the same dedicated server. The Host page can turn on a loopback domain listener. Copying the host command keeps the enabled packs and starts in the server's data folder.
- Set up DNS and HTTPS with the [domain hosting guide](../hosting-domain.md). It covers Caddy, a tunnel and direct UDP.
- Use **Server → Rules** to adjust combat, movement and progression during a match. Changes preserve health percentages and apply to all arenas. Save the profile from the process console to keep it across restarts.
- Occupied arenas can step concurrently on multicore hosts. Party rosters show ready markers and a shared count that resets each round.

## Combat and polish

- Bosses use distinct, clean hulls and readable cannon mounts. Special attacks lock their aim during the warning. Siege Engine, Skirmisher and Trapper each have their own weapons, movement and offline practice encounter.
- Credits scroll to the final line, including on smaller windows. Large custom maps bound particle and pad detail, and cache block style lookups.

**Multiplayer update:** This release uses protocol **24**. Upgrade the server and clients together. Versions 0.13 and earlier use an incompatible snapshot format.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.13.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.13.0

NVIDIA DLSS on GeForce RTX, a new opening that hands straight over to the menu, staff tools as private packs that survive updates, and a complete modding guide. Everything in [v0.12.0](v0.12.0.md) is included.

## Graphics

- **NVIDIA DLSS** on GeForce RTX GPUs, on Windows and Linux. DLSS Super Resolution rebuilds the arena from fewer pixels using its motion, and at 100% render scale it runs as DLAA, the sharpest anti-aliasing the game has. The render scale picks the mode (Performance, Balanced, Quality or DLAA). The DLSS runtime is a separate download the first time you choose it, checked against its SHA-256 before use. On RTX GPUs the Quality and Ultra presets use DLSS. Where DLSS can't run (an older GPU, an old driver), the Graphics tab says why and FSR 1 stands in.
- Laptops with two GPUs draw on the faster one: through the drivers' high-performance request on Windows, and through PRIME render offload on Linux when the NVIDIA GPU isn't driving the display. NVIDIA's Linux driver queues one frame ahead instead of up to three, for lower input latency. If a launch with these changes never opens a window, the next one starts without them, as does `--safe-graphics`.
- The Graphics tab names the GPU with its memory and driver, and warns in red when the system is rendering in software, which usually means the GPU driver is missing. On a Mac, it names the GPU Metal renders on.
- **Adaptive VSync** (Display tab, on by default with VSync, not on macOS): a frame that misses the display's refresh is shown at once instead of waiting a whole refresh, avoiding a stutter at the cost of a brief tear.

## Opening

- A two-second splash in the game's own style: the tank shoots three shapes and the name springs out of the bursts. The menu's live arena comes up behind it, and the menu takes over on the same arena without a cut, as does the staff password prompt.
- It notes what the game runs on, such as "Running on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 with NVIDIA DLSS" or "Running on Apple M2 Pro with Metal and MetalFX", with the trademark notices NVIDIA and Apple ask for. No logos are shown.
- Any key or click skips it. Modifier keys and shortcuts don't, so Cmd+Tab or taking a screenshot leaves it playing, and the key or click that skipped it never reaches the menu.
- With reduced motion, set in the game or in macOS or Windows, it fades without moving. On a Mac set to full screen, it waits for the window to finish moving into full screen before it plays.

## Staff tools

- Creator and central-owner tools now come as private **staff credential packs** published by Tankyard Moderation, in place of separately compiled editions. They're ordinary packs that every public build reads, so they keep working across updates without a private rebuild.
- Before anyone types a password, the game checks the pack's signature against the key built into every client, and refuses a pack that was changed or signed by anyone else. The password is asked for at every launch, and each wrong one doubles the wait before the next try. See [Staff credential packs](../creator-administration.md#staff-credential-packs).

## Mods

- The [modding guide](../modding.md) is rewritten in full: Luau (recommended) and legacy LuaJIT scripting with a migration guide, every event, query and command in the scripting API, HUD widgets, data packs, content, tools and troubleshooting.

Protocol **23**, as in v0.12: v0.13 and v0.12 clients and servers play together, and servers still welcome v0.10 and v0.11 clients.
